authority_blockers.reason: Exact formal M5 qualification parameters are not fully frozen: target hardware/workload identities and thresholds, security/vulnerability acceptance, package/install policy, upgrade/rollback, backup/restore and final release acceptance/signoff.

batches.name: Upgrade / rollback / recovery + formal release candidate

tasks.minimum_acceptance: Versioned machine authority freezes exact target hardware/workload identities, performance/resource thresholds, security/vulnerability acceptance, package/install rules, upgrade/rollback, backup/restore and formal Release acceptance criteria on protected main; implementation-local qualification constants are forbidden.

tasks.deliverable: P1-only formal qualification scope and claim guard
tasks.minimum_acceptance: M5 qualifies only existing P1 products; P2-P6 remain inactive; no artifact may claim formal M5 qualification before protected-main M5 Exit GO and exact evidence-manifest acceptance.

Project exactly WINDOWS_DESKTOP_X64, LINUX_DESKTOP_X64, WINDOWS_SERVICE_X64 and LINUX_SERVICE_X64 with their governed component inventories and fail-closed unsupported/degraded rules; no fifth implicit certification profile.

tasks.deliverable: Governed target hardware and workload-envelope projection
tasks.minimum_acceptance: Consume only approved target hardware/workload identities and workload-envelope schema/fixture hashes; every performance result binds exact build, profile, workload, baseline and dependency lock; missing authority fails closed.

Consume adopted security readiness, vulnerability acceptance, credential/config and artifact-integrity authority for all mandatory profiles; no local severity waiver or silent degraded security state.

Golden/negative tests prove exact four-profile inventory, authority hashes, workload/security binding, P1-only claims and fail-closed behavior when formal qualification authority is missing, mismatched or stale.

tasks.deliverable: Deterministic package/build provenance, SBOM and native-manifest production
tasks.minimum_acceptance: One semantic build version produces profile-bound package manifest, dependency lock, SBOM, native dependency manifest, source/Core/Catalog/schema hashes and artifact integrity/signing evidence exactly as adopted authority requires.

Each mandatory profile has governed clean install, READY/start, stop and uninstall evidence without developer-environment prerequisites; failure is atomic/fail-closed and preserves diagnostic evidence.

Required Windows Desktop components, GUI/local API/Worker/CLI/SQLite/Parquet-object access and governed filesystem/process behavior pass the adopted formal profile on approved environment and exact candidate build.

Required Linux Desktop components, GUI/local API/Worker/CLI/SQLite/Parquet-object access and governed filesystem/process behavior pass the adopted formal profile on approved environment and exact candidate build.
Required Windows Service API/Application, Worker, CLI/admin, PostgreSQL client and Parquet/object access pass the adopted formal profile on approved environment and exact candidate build.
Required Linux Service API/Application, Worker, CLI/admin, PostgreSQL client and Parquet/object access pass the adopted formal profile on approved environment and exact candidate build.
Approved workloads on required profiles meet adopted P50/P95/throughput/CPU/RSS/storage/concurrency limits; reports bind exact workload/profile/build hashes and may not widen thresholds on failure.
SBOM/dependency/native-manifest/vulnerability/integrity/signing checks meet adopted rules on every mandatory artifact; exceptions require governed authority and remain explicit in evidence.
One exact candidate SHA passes clean lifecycle, component smoke, full Golden/Replay subsets, workload performance/resource and security/artifact qualification for all four mandatory profiles.

Approved upgrade paths preserve DB schema compatibility, immutable Release/replay semantics and governed manifests; injected upgrade failure rolls back to a usable prior version without pointer/history corruption.

Approved backup/restore procedure meets adopted scope/target/evidence rules across applicable stores and profiles; restored state preserves release membership/provenance and fails closed on incomplete/corrupt backup.

tasks.deliverable: Formal release-candidate evidence manifest and signoff contract
tasks.minimum_acceptance: A versioned RC evidence manifest binds exact source revision, packages/hashes, authorities, schema/catalog/profile/workload/security evidence, replay lineage, upgrade/recovery results and required signoff identities; incomplete manifest cannot be accepted.

E2E and injected-failure fixtures prove governed upgrade, rollback, backup, restore, atomic failure behavior, exact historical Release/replay preservation and recovery evidence on applicable mandatory profiles.

tasks.deliverable: Formal release-candidate provenance and acceptance E2E
tasks.minimum_acceptance: The formal RC is reproducibly tied to exact source/baseline/dependencies/packages/SBOM/profile/workload/security/recovery evidence and satisfies adopted release-acceptance criteria without current/latest or environment-local substitutions.

tasks.deliverable: Same-candidate four-profile logical equivalence and qualification parity
tasks.minimum_acceptance: One candidate SHA proves Windows/Linux logical equivalence, exact Release/Replay semantics, all four mandatory profile results, governed numeric tolerances, performance/resource/security qualification and package evidence with only allowed physical differences.

Clean source+baseline+locked dependencies reconstruct formal artifacts and evidence manifest; clean install/readiness/replay/upgrade/recovery smoke passes without developer-local state on required profiles.

tasks.deliverable: M5 Exit review and formal P1 release decision
tasks.minimum_acceptance: Exact 23/23 M5 task evidence, four-profile qualification, governed workload/performance/security/package/upgrade/recovery/cold-start evidence and formal RC manifest all pass; failed_acceptance=[]; protected-main exact M5 Exit GO is required before any formal P1 release claim.
